Case study

Use the client’s view to make safer network decisions.

Wi-Fins-3MABGraph coloringSafe RL

The problem

Enterprise Wi-Fi changes on several timescales. Short interference bursts need fast, local reactions; channel assignments and power policies need slower, network-wide planning. Decisions must also respect service-level objectives for voice, exams, guests, streaming, and IoT traffic.

The system

The design expands the access point’s view with client measurements, transport-layer quality, and fine-time measurement. A fast loop detects airtime or interference spikes and applies bounded mitigation. A slow loop builds an interference graph, ranks channels with bandit feedback, and evaluates network-wide configurations.

Safety before deployment

A graph neural network predicts throughput, latency, and retry behavior for candidate states. Policies are checked against per-service constraints before being deployed; unsafe actions are rejected or rolled back. The GNN achieved errors of 7.4 percent on seen and 8.04 percent on unseen configurations in the report.

My contribution

I contributed to the adaptive decision pipeline, power estimation, simulation, and system integration, and presented the final work at the Inter-IIT Tech Meet hosted by IIT Patna.

Takeaway

Network intelligence is most useful when it is layered: fast controls for volatility, slower optimization for coordination, and explicit safeguards for real service requirements.
